title: Potential Divider
notes: **Definition:** two or more resistors in series across a voltage source, used to obtain a fraction of the source voltage.
**Output voltage:** $V_{out} = V_{in} \frac{R_2}{R_1 + R_2}$, where $R_2$ is the resistor across which the output is taken.
**Why useful:** allows you to set any voltage between 0 and $V_{in}$ by adjusting the ratio of resistances.
**Loading effect:** if a load resistor $R_L$ is connected across $R_2$, the output voltage changes because $R_2$ is now in parallel with $R_L$, reducing the effective resistance.
**Potentiometer:** a continuous potential divider using a uniform resistance wire. The output voltage is proportional to the length of wire between the wiper and one end.
